identity.real_world_identity_notes: Lamborghini identifies the EVO2 as part of the six-speed sequential Huracan GT3 lineage. The exact base AMS2 identity was guided-tested; Low Downforce is an explicit aero-package alias inheriting the base controls and was not separately tested.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim without an integrated display or wheel-mounted shift lights.

notes: The base car moved from rest without physical clutch input; the underlying simulator mechanism was not established.
Six paddle-selected gears, clutchless no-lift upshifts, and clutchless downshifts with automatic blip were directly established.
A brief throttle-channel interruption was later found insufficient to establish automatic ignition cut; that field remains unknown.
The Low Downforce identity inherits base controls as an explicit untested aero-package assumption.
Guided base-car test completed in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch and Auto Shifting disabled.
The base identity, clutch-free move-off, six paddle gears, automatic blip, and closed no-display rim were directly observed.
The throttle-channel dip could reflect driver input, traction control, or telemetry filtering, so automatic cut remains unknown.
Low Downforce inherits these controls as an untested aero-package assumption.

confidence.basis: Exact identity and the established user-facing controls were directly verified; manufacturer sources support the GT3 EVO2 identity and six-speed sequential lineage. Automatic cut is not established.

notes: Observed live in ACC 21257365 via guided verification observation acc.lamborghini-hurac-n-gt3-evo2-2023.20260823t013248499z-d585ec4d by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Lamborghini establishes the GT3 EVO2 identity and transmission lineage. ACC reported the exact GT3 Evo2, 2023 year, stable internal id and GT3 class; the guided drive directly established ACC behavior.

claims.basis: Official simulator and manufacturer sources agree with the exact live telemetry identity and class.
Low Downforce is an exact observed identity whose controls explicitly inherit the tested base as an aero-package assumption.
Lamborghini lineage documentation and direct exercise of all six paddle-selected gears agree.
Guided current-game testing and cockpit inspection directly established these values.
Telemetry name `Lamborghini Huracán GT3 Evo2 2023`, internal id `lamborghini_huracan_gt3_evo2`, and class `GT3` distinguish the car from the Super Trofeo EVO2 already covered in ACC.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic blip, and the cockpit rim; automatic cut remained unknown.

notes: Low Downforce is an explicit inherited alias and was not separately live-tested.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
driver_summary: Paddle sequential that gets away without a clutch and blips its own downshifts. Whether it cuts the upshift was not established by the drive, so lift as though it does not.
